evidence.curator_note: Substrate as drawn: the 2-ethylhexanal molecular ion, labelled 'm/z 128' under the structure. The skeleton is printed as C2H5-CH(H)-CH2-CH(C2H5)-CHO with the gamma hydrogen on C4 drawn EXPLICITLY, an aldehyde H on C1, and '+.' printed above the carbonyl oxygen. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the charge and odd electron are written on the oxygen exactly where the page prints them, [CH:1]=[O+:7], not carried only in the JSON fields. Fourth channel: the arrow labelled with an italic 'i' running down-right to the FORMULA 'C4H9(C2H5)CH+ / m/z 99'. Charge-site-initiated (inductive) cleavage of the same C1-C2 bond that the alpha channel breaks, but with the charge MIGRATING to the alkyl fragment: C7H15+ (99.1168) plus the neutral formyl radical HC=O., the complement of the alpha channel's HC≡O+ / C7H15. pair. Book draws 0 arc(s) and NO product structure -- only the condensed formula -- so both moves are curator-supplied. ENCODING (the reason this is two one-electron moves and not one two-electron arrow): the precursor is an ODD-ELECTRON ion whose charge and radical both sit on oxygen, while the products are an even-electron cation and a neutral radical. The oxygen must therefore END neutral and spin-paired, so one electron of the breaking C1-C2 bond pairs with the oxygen's odd electron (move <1>) and the other stays on C1 as the formyl radical's unpaired electron (move <2>); C2, having lost both, becomes the cation. A single 2-electron arrow cannot express that, because it would leave the oxygen charged.
